title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-2
notes:
West leads the ♠8 against 3NT. West's lead is won by South with the ♠J. There are 7 top tricks (the spade trick just won, 3 hearts, 2 diamonds, and the ♣A). South should try to develop 2 extra tricks in diamonds.

This will only be possible if diamonds are 3-3. South will have to lose the lead in diamonds and he should gear his play towards losing a diamond trick to West. Should East gain the lead in diamonds, the defense might be in a position to cash 4 spade tricks.

South should lead a diamond at trick 2. If West plays the ♦Q, he is allowed to hold the trick. West will be unable to attack spades profitably from his side of the table.

If West follows small, the diamond trick is won in dummy. South crosses in hearts and plays another diamond. If West plays the ♦Q, he is allowed to win, as before. If West follows small the trick is won in dummy. A diamond trick is now conceded. If West was dealt the ♦Q he will be forced to win the trick. As long as diamonds are 3-3 the contract will be safe. The ♥K will be an entry to the long diamonds in dummy.

This deal looks superficially similar to the last one (C-1). Both deals involve establishing the diamond suit for 4 tricks. In this deal, South must play to keep the defender to the right of the long suit off lead. In the previous deal, now shown above, South had to play to keep the defender to the left of the long suit off lead.
